title: Aba-Seq
scope: Illumina single-route explanatory schematic for bulk AbaSI-coupled 5hmC mapping, interpreted with the supplied Sun et al. primary full text (PMID 23352666). It depicts glucosylation, AbaSI cleavage, biotinylated end-adaptor ligation, fragmentation and streptavidin capture, ending at DNA. Primary-supported library completion and readout are explicit interfaces, not claimed visible substeps. Catalogue-named scAba-seq and the distinct PvuRts1I related method are assessed separately at the supplied abstract evidence level; their detailed library architectures are not merged into this route.

states.label: Hydroxymethylated genomic DNA
features: The biological target is 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) in DNA, drawn as red dots; the far-left highlighted-residue icon is explanatory, with no separate material-transfer arrow.
The primary implementation uses mouse E14 embryonic stem-cell genomic DNA; the schematic itself does not specify a specimen or a single-cell compartment.

evidence.locator: Far-left explanatory legend: 5hmc residues; AbaSI coupled with sequencing (Aba-seq) to map high-resolution hydroxymethylome (5hmC). Highlighted red sites are a target summary, not a separate preparation branch.
Hydroxy-methyl-ated DNA: blue DNA line with red modification dots, immediately before T4-βGT.
[b00008] Introduction, concluding paragraph
evidence.quote: Here we report the genome-wide high-resolution hydroxymethylome of the mouse E14 ESCs using AbaSI-coupled sequencing (Aba-seq).

states.label: Glucosylated 5-hmC DNA (5gmC)
features: T4 β-glucosyltransferase converts DNA 5hmC to glucosylated 5hmC, called 5gmC in the primary paper.
Blue flag-like symbols at the marked sites denote the depicted glucosylation state; these are not evidence of biotinylation of the modified base.

evidence.locator: T4-βGT arrow from hydroxymethylated DNA to Glucosylated 5-hmC; blue flag-like marks appear at red sites.
[b00011] Results: Aba-seq and 5hmC Site Validation
evidence.quote: Conversion of genomic 5hmC to 5gmC was completed by using the T4 β-glucosyltransferase

states.label: AbaSI-cleaved genomic DNA
features: Double-stranded DNA fragments carry AbaSI-generated cut ends at a narrow range of distances from recognized 5gmC.
The important information carrier is the cleavage boundary relative to the original modified site; the schematic does not resolve cut-end chemistry.

evidence.locator: Glucosylated 5-hmC → AbaSI → separated blue duplex fragments.
[b00011] Results: AbaSI recognition and cleavage
evidence.quote: DNA modification-dependent restriction endonuclease AbaSI recognizes 5gmC with high specificity and generates double-stranded breaks at the 3′ side of the binding sites

evidence.locator: [b00012] Results: inference of putative 5hmC sites
evidence.quote: Putative 5hmC sites can be deduced by checking the presence of cytosine at expected distances (N13/N11,N12/N10,N11/N9) from either side of the mapped cleavage sites

states.label: Biotinylated primers (diagram label); P1b DNA adaptor (primary identification)
features: The incoming short magenta/blue reagent is resolved as biotinylated DNA adaptor P1b, with a randomized two-base 3′ overhang.
Biotin is carried on the DNA adaptor; no atom-level placement or extra end-group formula is inferred from the icon.

states.label: Genomic DNA bearing biotinylated P1b at AbaSI ends

The same adaptor associates an AbaSI cleavage boundary with a capture handle and the eventual sequencing-entry end.

states.label: Fragmented P1b-ligated DNA mixture
features: The Fragment panel contains tagged terminal fragments and bare interior fragments.
Terminal pieces retain an original P1b-marked AbaSI end and acquire a fragmentation-generated opposite end; sonication is identified by the primary paper.

states.label: Bead-bound biotin-P1b-bearing DNA fragments
features: Tagged DNA is attached to streptavidin magnetic beads through the biotin capture handle.
Selection acts on the adaptor tag. Its association with 5hmC is provided by upstream glucosylation-dependent AbaSI cleavage, rather than by direct recognition of 5hmC at the bead.

states.label: Nonretained DNA from the fragmentation mixture (implicit selection outcome)
features: Includes untagged interior fragments, which lack the intended biotin capture handle and do not form the retained library route.

states.label: Aba-seq DNA library (primary-supported interpretation of terminal DNA)
features: Illumina ends with a DNA icon; it does not explicitly draw a complete adapter configuration or an amplification step.
The primary implementation completes the captured inserts with P2 and amplifies with P1b/P2-specific primers, yielding a library separated from beads.
Genomic insert sequences and their P1b-derived ends carry the cleavage-boundary association in the final library.

evidence.rationale: Establishes the broad completion interface after capture; the Illumina schematic does not depict these as individual operations.

evidence.locator: [b00011] Results: read initiation and genomic mapping
evidence.quote: Sequencing was initiated from the P1b end, and the AbaSI cleavage sites were revealed after mapping the reads to the reference genome.
evidence.rationale: Mapping sequences initiated at P1b recovers the cleavage boundary; the positional association is carried by the library sequence and entry end rather than by directly reading the chemical modification.

states.label: Mapped cleavage sites and putative genomic 5hmC locations
features: DNA sequence read from the P1b end identifies AbaSI cleavage coordinates after reference mapping; nearby cytosines at expected offsets provide candidate original 5hmC positions.
High resolution does not mean unique base assignment at every site: the original study reports ambiguity for 13% of its identified cleavage sites.
The map is conditioned on enzyme recognition, cleavage efficiency and library selection. It is not a direct measurement of 5mC or proof that all 5hmC sites were captured.

operations.label: T4-βGT
operations.description: Acts on hydroxymethylated genomic DNA and converts its 5hmC residues to the glucosylated state shown as Glucosylated 5-hmC.
operations.mechanism: T4 β-glucosyltransferase glucosylates DNA 5hmC to 5gmC; the enzyme label denotes a catalyst, not a transferred DNA intermediate.
operations.information_effect: Preserves the genomic locations of the target while creating the modification state preferentially recognized by AbaSI.

operations.label: AbaSI
operations.description: Acts on glucosylated genomic DNA and generates double-stranded breaks near recognized 5gmC, yielding the separated duplex fragments drawn after the arrow.
operations.mechanism: AbaSI makes offset double-stranded cuts after recognition of 5gmC. The primary study reports no digestion of 5mC or C under its conditions, and different cleavage efficiencies depending on the arrangement of cytosines around the cut.
operations.information_effect: Encodes a nearby modification as a mappable DNA boundary. Cleavage is an enzyme-dependent sampling step, so the surviving library is not an unbiased census of every modified base.

operations.label: Ligate
operations.description: Acts on AbaSI-cleaved DNA and the incoming biotinylated oligonucleotide reagent; ligation produces DNA bearing tagged P1b ends. The diagram calls the reagent Biotinylated primers; the primary paper identifies a DNA adaptor.
operations.mechanism: Biotinylated P1b with a randomized two-base 3′ overhang is ligated to the AbaSI-digested DNA.
operations.information_effect: Couples the AbaSI cut end to both the biotin capture handle and the sequencing-entry interface. It does not biotinylate the genomic 5hmC residue.

operations.label: Fragment
operations.description: Acts on the already P1b-ligated DNA and shortens it, producing the depicted mixture of tagged terminal fragments and untagged interior DNA.
operations.mechanism: The Illumina arrow is generic fragmentation; the primary Figure 1B caption specifies sonication after P1b ligation.
operations.information_effect: Retains the marked AbaSI end in tagged pieces while creating the opposite insert end used by the downstream library interface.

operations.label: Streptavidin magnetic bead pull down
operations.description: Acts on the fragmented mixture and retains biotin-P1b-bearing DNA on streptavidin beads. Untagged interior fragments lack the intended capture handle and constitute an implicit nonretained fraction.
operations.mechanism: Biotin-bearing P1-ligated DNA associates with streptavidin magnetic beads. The bead is the capture support, not a separate genomic substrate or a second modification detector.
operations.information_effect: Enriches DNA bearing an original tagged AbaSI boundary. Bead attachment is a consequential material state; the selection itself does not establish perfect biological specificity.

operations.label: DNA — library completion interface (primary text; compressed in diagram)
operations.description: Connects the bead-bound selected fragments to the terminal DNA product. The primary implementation prepares the free ends on beads, adds adaptor P2, and amplifies with P1b/P2-specific primers to yield a library separated from the beads. These are represented as one broad completion block because Illumina draws only the final arrow and DNA icon.
operations.mechanism: The primary Figure 1B caption and library-construction text establish the second-adaptor and amplification interface after capture; these internal operations are not individually depicted in the supplied schematic.
operations.information_effect: Creates a sequenceable DNA library whose P1b-derived end preserves the cleavage-boundary association. Amplification transfers this information into library copies.

operations.label: Sequencing from P1b and cleavage-site interpretation (primary text)
operations.description: Sequences the DNA library from the P1b end, maps the reads to the reference genome, and uses cytosines at expected offsets from mapped AbaSI cuts to infer putative 5hmC locations. This explains the readout promised by the far-left legend; no sequencer or analysis panel is drawn.
operations.mechanism: The readout carrier is genomic DNA sequence with an identifiable P1b entry boundary. The target modification is inferred from cleavage position and nearby sequence, rather than directly decoded as a modified base during ordinary DNA sequencing.
operations.information_effect: Produces high-resolution candidate 5hmC positions, including ambiguous assignments in the reported dataset. The original study reports differential cutting efficiencies and some sites compatible with more than one candidate cytosine.
